original_value: This paper explores the possibility of tracking finger drawings in the air leveraging WiFi signals from commodity devices. Prior solutions typically require user to hold a wireless transmitter, or need proprietary wireless hardware. They can only recognize a small set of pre-defined hand gestures. This paper introduces FingerDraw, the first sub-wavelength level finger motion tracking system using commodity WiFi devices, without attaching any sensor to finger. FingerDraw can reconstruct finger drawing trajectory such as digits, alphabets, and symbols with the setting of one WiFi transmitter and two WiFi receivers. It uses a two-antenna receiver to sense the sub-wavelength scale displacement of finger motion in each direction. The theoretical underpinning of FingerDraw is our proposed CSI-quotient model, which uses the channel quotient between two antennas of the receiver to cancel out the noise in CSI amplitude and the random offsets in CSI phase, and quantifies the correlation between CSI value dynamics and object displacement. This channel quotient is sensitive to and enables us to detect small changes in In-phase and Quadrature parts of channel state information due to finger movement. Our experimental results show that the overall median tracking accuracy is 1.27 cm, and the recognition of drawing ten digits in the air achieves an average accuracy of over 93.0%.

result.paraphrase: This paper investigates tracking finger drawings in the air using WiFi signals from commodity devices. Earlier methods usually force the user to hold a wireless transmitter or rely on proprietary wireless hardware, and they can recognize only a limited set of pre-defined hand gestures. We present FingerDraw, the first sub-wavelength finger-motion tracking system based on commodity WiFi devices, with no sensor attached to the finger. With one WiFi transmitter and two WiFi receivers, FingerDraw can reconstruct finger-drawing trajectories including digits, letters, and symbols. It employs a two-antenna receiver to sense sub-wavelength displacement of finger motion in each direction. FingerDraw is built on our proposed CSI-quotient model, which takes the channel quotient between the receiver’s two antennas to remove CSI amplitude noise and random CSI phase offsets, while characterizing the correlation between CSI dynamics and object displacement. This channel quotient is sensitive enough to detect small changes in the in-phase and quadrature components of channel state information caused by finger movement. Experiments show a median overall tracking accuracy of 1.27 cm, and average recognition accuracy above 93.0% for drawing ten digits in the air.
